HON.rationale: HON is facing a severe fundamental deterioration that the market has not yet fully priced in. Q1 2026 showed a dramatic earnings collapse: EPS fell 41.9% YoY to $1.29 (from $2.22 in Q1 2025) and 47.3% QoQ (from $2.45 in Q2 2025). Net income dropped45.8% YoY. Operating cash flow swung to -$650M from +$597M a year ago, a -208.9% YoY deterioration. Revenue growth was a tepid +2.4% YoY, missing consensus by 1.4%. The balance sheet is deteriorating: total equity shrank from $18.02B (Q1 2025) to $14.67B (Q1 2026), while total debt grew from $27.08B to $32.11B, pushing debt-to-equity to 2.19x. ROE has declined from 31.7% to 28% and net margin from 15.1% to 10.9% over the past year. Despite this earnings collapse, the stock has rallied and now trades at a P/E of 36.0x — the top of its 12-month range (21.6–37.0) and 47% above the ~24.5x level of June 2025 when earnings were far stronger. P/B has expanded from 7.8x to 10.1x. The company is trading at peak multiples on trough earnings — a dangerous combination. The aerospace spinoff (June 29, 2026) introduces significant execution risk, estimated $1.5–2.0B in separation costs, and uncertainty about the post-spin RemainCo's ability to deliver on 4–6% organic growth and 10%+ EPS growth targets. Full-year revenue guidance slightly missed expectations. The macro backdrop offers no support: 10Y Treasury yields at 4.4%, elevated rate environment, and rising initial jobless claims (216K latest). News sentiment is mixed-to-positive (mean 0.59) but the fundamental picture is deteriorating rapidly. This is a classic case of a company with worsening fundamentals, expensive valuation, and near-term downside catalyst (post-spinoff reality check).
